title: Work & colleagues
goal: Chat with colleagues, talk about deadlines and meetings, ask your boss for leave, write a formal email and get through a job interview.
intro:
Nepali offices run on a mix of Nepali and English: you'll hear **डेडलाइन**, **रिपोर्ट**, **मिटिङ** and **प्रमोसन** in every other sentence, wrapped in Nepali grammar and Nepali politeness. This unit is about getting that politeness right: **तपाईं** with colleagues, **सर / म्याडम** and honorific verbs for the boss, **हजुर** when a senior calls you, and the stiff written style (**आदरणीय सर… अनुरोध गर्दछु**) of formal emails and notices.

You'll also learn the **passive** — **मिटिङ सारियो** 'the meeting has been moved', **निर्णय गरियो** 'it was decided' — which is how offices talk about things that happen without saying who did them.

grammar.title: Formal register: talking to and about the boss, and writing formally
grammar.body:
**Who gets which 'you'.** At work the default is **तपाईं** — with colleagues too, even ones your own age, until someone suggests तिमी. A boss who is much older or very senior may get **हजुर**; it takes the same verb forms as तपाईं (-नुहुन्छ, -नुभयो, -नुहोस्). Talking **about** seniors you use उहाँ-style honorific verbs: सर **आउनुभयो** 'sir has arrived', म्याडम मिटिङमा **हुनुहुन्छ**. Using आयो or छ for your boss sounds like you're talking about a junior.

**What you call people.** Seniors are **सर / म्याडम** (English loans used in every Nepali office) or name + **जी** (विकासजी). Colleagues a bit older are **दाइ / दिदी**, younger ones **भाइ / बहिनी**. When a senior calls you or asks for something, answer **हजुर** 'yes? / certainly'. Seniors often use तिमी with juniors, who still answer with तपाईं.

**Asking a senior for something.** Climb the ladder from unit 18: **दिनुहोस्** → **दिनुहुन्छ कि?** → **दिन मिल्छ?** 'is it possible to…?'. To ask permission for yourself, use the optative **पाऊँ** 'may I get': **बिदा पाऊँ** 'may I have leave', **कुरा गर्न पाऊँ?** 'may I have a word?'. Give the reason with **-एकोले** 'because': सन्चो **नभएकोले** 'because I'm not well'.

**Written formal style.** Emails, letters and notices use a different set of forms. The present tense becomes **-दछ / -दछु / -दछौँ** (गर्**दछु** 'I do', जान्**दछ** 'he knows'). A request to someone is **-नुहुन अनुरोध छ** 'you are kindly requested to…'. Letters open with **आदरणीय सर / म्याडम** and end with **धन्यवाद**. Nobody *says* गर्दछु to a colleague — it sounds like the evening news.

grammar.title: The passive: 'it was decided', 'it has been moved'
grammar.body:
Nepali makes a passive by adding **-इ-** to the verb stem and then using the ordinary endings. The verb then agrees with the **thing**, not with a person:

गर्नु → **गरिन्छ** 'is done' · **गरियो** 'was done' · **गरिएको छ** 'has been done' · **गरिनेछ** 'will be done' · negative **गरिँदैन** 'isn't done', **गरिएन** 'wasn't done'.
Vowel stems add -इ- too: पठाउनु → **पठाइयो** 'was sent', बोलाउनु → **बोलाइयो**, दिनु → **दिइयो**, लिनु → **लिइयो**.

You have met this already: **यहाँ फोटो खिच्न पाइन्छ?** 'may one take photos here?' and **सकिन्छ** 'it can be done'.

Use it when **who** did it doesn't matter, or you'd rather not say: मिटिङ **सारियो** 'the meeting has been postponed', निर्णय **गरियो** 'it was decided', सबैलाई इमेल **पठाइयो** 'an email was sent to everyone'. Official notices are full of it: **सूचना गरिन्छ** 'notice is hereby given', **…गरिनेछ** 'will be done'.

To name the doer, formal Nepali uses **-बाट** or **-द्वारा** 'by': हाकिमबाट स्वीकृत गरियो 'approved by the manager'. In everyday speech people simply use the active with ले: हाकिमले स्वीकृत गर्नुभयो.

**Impersonal** uses of the same form are everywhere: **भनिन्छ** 'they say, it is said', **के गरिन्छ?** 'what can you do?', **जान सकिँदैन** 'you can't go'.

The trap: in a passive sentence the thing is the subject, so it never takes ले: **मिटिङ** सारियो, not ~~मिटिङले~~ सारियो.

examples.en: Today's meeting has been moved to Monday.

dialogue.title: Monday morning at the office
dialogue.setting: A software company in Baneshwor, Kathmandu. Puja arrives late; her older colleague Bikash fills her in. Later she goes to see their manager, Sharma sir.

lines.native: ओहो पूजा, आज ढिलो? जाम थियो?
lines.roman: oho Pujā, āja ḍhilo? jām thiyo?

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.native: के भन्नु दाइ, कोटेश्वरमा आधा घण्टा जाम!
lines.roman: ke bhannu dāi, Koṭeswarmā ādhā ghanṭā jām!
lines.en: Don’t ask, dai — half an hour stuck at Koteshwor!

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.en: Don't worry, the morning meeting got postponed.

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.en: Phew, saved! Why was it moved?

lines.speaker: Bikash

lines.roman: klāinṭle projekṭko ḍeḍlāin baḍhāune kurā garechha.
lines.en: Turns out the client wants to talk about extending the project deadline.

lines.native: साँच्चै? त्यसो भए रिपोर्ट शुक्रबारसम्म पठाए पुग्छ?
lines.roman: sāṃchchai? tyaso bhae riporṭ sukrabārsamma paṭhāe pugchha?
lines.en: Really? So it's enough if I send the report by Friday?

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: हो जस्तो छ। तर सरलाई एकपटक सोध्नू है।
lines.roman: ho jasto chha. tara sarlāi ekpaṭak sodhnu hai.
lines.en: Looks like it. But do check with sir.

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.en: Sir, may I have a quick word?

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.native: रिपोर्ट शुक्रबार पठाए हुन्छ? अनि अर्को बिहीबार मलाई एक दिनको बिदा चाहिएको थियो।
lines.roman: riporṭ sukrabār paṭhāe hunchha? ani arko bihibār malāi ek dinko bidā chāhieko thiyo.
lines.en: Is it OK to send the report on Friday? And I was hoping for a day's leave next Thursday.

lines.speaker: Mr Sharma
lines.native: शुक्रबार भए हुन्छ। बिदाको लागि एउटा इमेल पठाउनुहोस्, म स्वीकृत गरिदिन्छु।
lines.roman: sukrabār bhae hunchha. bidāko lāgi euṭā imel paṭhāunuhos, ma swikrit garidinchhu.
lines.en: Friday's fine. Send me an email about the leave and I'll approve it.

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.en: Well? Did you get the leave?

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.native: पाएँ! तर पहिले इमेल लेख्नुपर्छ — "आदरणीय सर, सविनय अनुरोध छ…"
lines.roman: pāeṃ! tara pahile imel lekhnuparchha — "ādaraniya sar, sabinaya anurodh chha…"
lines.en: Yes! But first I have to write the email — "Respected Sir, I humbly request…"

culture:
The working week in Nepal runs **Sunday to Friday**; Saturday is the weekly holiday, though many private firms, especially in IT and NGOs, give Sunday off too. Offices open around ten, and the tea break (**चिया खाने बेला**) is where the real conversations happen.

Titles matter. In private companies seniors are **सर** and **म्याडम**; in government offices you hear **हजुर** constantly; colleagues become **दाइ, दिदी, भाइ, बहिनी**. Seniors often use तिमी with juniors, who answer with तपाईं — that's normal, not rude. A first name alone for an older colleague sounds disrespectful, so add **जी** (विकासजी) if in doubt.

Government offices post notices in very formal Nepali (**सूचना**, **-दछ**, **गरिनेछ**), and getting anything done there can mean a queue, a stamp and someone who hasn't signed the attendance register (**हाजिर**) yet. Private-sector email is often in English, but a leave request in formal Nepali to an older boss is appreciated. Many young Nepalis spend years preparing for the **लोकसेवा** (civil service) exams, and **विदेश जाने** — going abroad to work or study — is a constant topic at the tea break.

lessons.title: Small talk with colleagues

tip.title: Talking to and about people at work
tip.body:
- Default at work: **तपाईं** — even with colleagues your age, until they suggest तिमी.
- Seniors: **सर / म्याडम** or name + **जी**; a bit older: **दाइ / दिदी**.
- Talking *about* a senior: honorific verbs **-नुहुन्छ / -नुभयो**: सर आउ**नुभयो**, म्याडम व्यस्त **हुनुहुन्छ**.

tip.title: Getting it done: -इसक्नु and -सम्म
tip.body:
- Stem + **-इसक्नु** = 'finish doing, have it done': पठा**इसक्छु** 'I'll have it sent', गर**िसक्यौ?** 'have you done it yet?'.
- **-सम्म** 'by, until': शुक्रबार**सम्म** 'by Friday', कहिले**सम्म** 'by when?'.
- 'Not yet': **अझै गरेको छैन**.

sentences.en: Have you sent the report yet? (to a colleague you call तिमी)
I've already sent the email.
By when does this project have to be finished?
The report has to be submitted by Monday.

sentences.native: यो काम मेरो जिम्मेवारी हो, म गरिसक्छु।

sentences.en: This job is my responsibility — I'll get it done.
Have you submitted the project report yet?

sentences.roman: ḍeḍlāin bholi ho, āja rāti kām garnuparchha.
sentences.en: The deadline's tomorrow, so I have to work tonight.

sentences.native: अझै गरेको छैन, दस मिनेटमा पठाउँछु।

sentences.en: Not yet — I'll send it in ten minutes.

sentences.roman: yo imel sabai ṭimlāi paṭhāidinuhos na.
sentences.en: Could you send this email to the whole team?

tip.title: Passive: 'it was done'
tip.body:
- Stem + **-इ-** + ending: गर्नु → **गरियो** 'was done', **गरिन्छ** 'is done', **गरिनेछ** 'will be done'.
- Vowel stems too: पठा**इयो** 'was sent'; सार्नु → **सारियो** 'was moved'.
- The *thing* is the subject, so no ले: **मिटिङ** सारियो, not मिटिङले.

lessons.title: Asking the boss for leave

tip.title: Asking a senior politely
tip.body:
- Ask permission with **पाऊँ** 'may I get': बिदा **पाऊँ**, कुरा गर्न **पाऊँ**?
- Or **-न मिल्छ?** 'is it OK to…?': चाँडो जा**न मिल्छ**?
- Give the reason with **-एकोले** 'because': सन्चो **नभएकोले**…
- When a senior calls you, answer **हजुर**.

tip.title: Formal writing: आदरणीय…, -दछु
tip.body:
- Letters and emails open with **आदरणीय सर / म्याडम**.
- 'I do' becomes **-दछु**: अनुरोध गर्**दछु** 'I request', जानकारी गराउँ**दछु** 'I inform you'.
- 'You are requested to…': **-नुहुन अनुरोध छ**.
- Spoken Nepali never uses -दछु — to a colleague it sounds like the news.

sentences.native: आदरणीय सर, म तीन दिनको बिदाको लागि अनुरोध गर्दछु।
sentences.roman: ādaraniya sar, ma tin dinko bidāko lāgi anurodh gardachhu.
sentences.en: Dear Sir, I request three days' leave.
